decisions.statement: A value is put after the values a property already has where that property says nothing of order.
A value is put into the place that order asks for where the property says its values are sorted.
A value naming a page that is not there refuses the answer.
Whether a property has many values is read from the body rather than from the type.
A property holding one value is refused rather than made a list.
Putting a second value into a property with one value is a restatement.
A value the property has already is refused rather than held twice.
A page stating no such key gains that key rather than being refused.
A key is judged before the body is read.
A key spelled as a slug is refused rather than gained under that spelling.
The refusal names the key that spelling makes.
A key that is no bare word is refused rather than gained.
A key the page gains is written after the property `after` names.
An `after` naming no property the page states is refused rather than dropped.
A key the page gains is written last where no `after` is stated.
An `after` stated where the page states the key already is refused rather than dropped.
A body exporting no object is refused rather than gaining a key.
The body is answered rather than written.
The passage answered is the lines the value is put into rather than the body.
Whether a key is sorted is worked out by the module this change names.
The shapes are one answer held for the change rather than a page opened for each value.
Nothing here walks the index, opens a page, or looks for a path.
A key the page gains has one value where the caller says the property has one.
A key the page gains is a list where the caller says nothing about the property.
The literal a value is written as is worked out by the module this change names.
A value that kind does not hold is refused before the body is read.

definition: one value put into one page property in a page's body
